Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Markets-focused coverage dominates right now: outlets are converging on the Houthi strike on Saudi Aramco's headquarters and its ripple effects on aviation and oil, a record $1.2 billion Treasury penalty against Bank of America, and the wait for the September U.S. CPI report just ahead of the Fed's next meeting. Bank earnings season, AI-bubble jitters after a failed Australian IPO, and China's surging trade surplus round out the major threads.

stories.headline: Houthi Strike Hits Saudi Aramco Headquarters
stories.summary: An attack on Aramco's headquarters follows earlier strikes on Riyadh's international airport, marking an expansion of the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi militants.

stories.headline: Bank of America Fined $1.2 Billion for Money-Laundering Failures
stories.summary: Treasury regulators imposed more than $1.2 billion in penalties — the third-largest in department history — after finding Bank of America failed to report over $5 billion in suspicious transactions, including ones tied to Chinese money-laundering networks and sanctioned countries.

stories.headline: Investors Brace for Key September CPI Report
stories.summary: Markets are awaiting the CPI release, with economists expecting headline inflation up 0.6% on the month and 3.6% annually, a reading that could shape the Fed's rate decision in two weeks.

stories.headline: Rising Rates Cloud Otherwise Strong Bank Earnings
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan posted higher quarterly profits, but Wall Street's mood is turning more cautious as rising rates loom over the sector, with smaller private-equity firms already feeling the pain.

stories.headline: China's Exports Surge, Trade Surplus on Track for Record
stories.summary: China's exports grew last month at the fastest pace in almost any month since the global financial crisis, pushing its trade surplus toward a record.

stories.headline: Failed Australian IPO Sends Shockwaves Through AI Trade
stories.summary: The collapse of what would have been Australia's largest IPO in decades is making data-center startups and other tech firms rethink their public-listing timing amid high rates and political uncertainty.

stories.headline: Starlink Speed Limits Disrupt Ukraine's War Effort
stories.summary: Ukrainian military units and officials say a new speed limit on Elon Musk's Starlink network is hampering drone attacks on Russian-occupied territory.

stories.headline: Riyadh Airport Attacks Disrupt Global Aviation
stories.summary: Deadly attacks at Riyadh's main airport are disrupting airlines and closing airspace, prompting Delta to delay its planned first-ever nonstop U.S.-Saudi route until March and the FAA to warn carriers of safety risks.

Business.gaps: No recent business-relevant items were found for The Information or Puck beyond entertainment/media newsletter content; Forbes and Fortune surfaced mostly markets-data and leadership features rather than hard breaking news.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on a volatile Middle East backdrop rattling oil markets, a fresh Trump administration push against offshore wind permitting, and a string of U.S. grid/data-center regulatory fights playing out at FERC and in state utility hearings. Affordability — rising electricity bills and wildfire-driven shutoffs in California — remains a recurring thread across Heatmap, Utility Dive and Bloomberg.

stories.headline: Houthi strike hits building at Saudi Aramco headquarters
stories.summary: Iran-backed Houthi militants struck Saudi Aramco's headquarters in apparent retaliation after a Riyadh-led coalition hit sites in Yemen's capital, expanding the conflict beyond Yemen into the kingdom's energy infrastructure.

stories.headline: Oil prices spike as Saudi attacks overshadow Russian diesel deal
stories.summary: News of a Trump administration deal with Russia to pump diesel into the global market should have eased oil prices, but instead all three major crude benchmarks spiked Monday by nearly 1.5%, with only U.S. WTI staying below $100 a barrel.

stories.headline: FERC rejects most of PJM's large-load interconnection plan
stories.summary: Federal regulators found that PJM's plan for curtailing large loads lacking matching new generation intrudes on state jurisdiction and appears discriminatory, dealing a setback to the grid operator's approach to managing data-center demand.

stories.headline: TotalEnergies buys $1.2B of U.S. solar farms after quitting offshore wind
stories.summary: TotalEnergies took more than $1 billion from the Trump administration to kill off its offshore wind projects, but its joint venture with KKR has now announced a deal to add 700 megawatts of solar to its portfolio. The $1.2 billion acquisition includes three utility-scale solar farms in Texas and Ohio expected online in the first quarter of next year.

stories.headline: PG&E warns of more shutoffs as fire conditions threaten California grid
stories.summary: PG&E cautioned that planned power shutoffs could hit more than two dozen counties in northern and central California and continue through the weekend as wildfire risk persists.

stories.headline: Dominion-NextEra merger hearing zeroes in on rates and data centers
stories.summary: A local hearing on the proposed Dominion-NextEra merger focused on rate impacts and data-center-driven demand, with regulators pressing on past commitments Dominion made under Virginia's clean-energy law.

stories.headline: FERC approves Duke's large-load transmission rules despite cost-shift concerns
stories.summary: FERC approved Duke Energy Carolinas' proposal for handling large new loads, though a commissioner warned that consumer protections against cost-shifting remain inadequate nationally and further action may be needed.

Energy.gaps: Canary Media and E&E News searches returned only evergreen/about-page content rather than fresh stories (E&E News appears to have stopped publishing standalone articles after August 31, migrating to POLITICO Pro). Latitude Media's most recent relevant item found was from October 9 (slightly outside the 48-hour window). Argus Media and Carbon Brief (beyond the COP17 biodiversity item in the feed) could not be checked due to search limits; Reuters, The Economist, NYT and WSJ were only available via the provided feed items, which contained no energy-specific lead stories from Reuters or additional NYT/Economist pieces beyond what's cited above.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: African outlets are converging on health and security crises — the DRC's Ebola outbreak topping 9,000 cases and a new case scare in Kenya — alongside political upheaval in Nigeria and Mauritius, and fresh scrutiny of Nigeria's security strategy, ICC pressure tied to Navi Pillay's Nobel win, and Algeria-UAE diplomatic fallout. Business and tech coverage focuses on Microsoft's Nairobi retreat, fintech competition in Kenya, and continued mining investment confidence in South Africa.

stories.headline: DRC Ebola outbreak passes 9,000 cases, over 4,000 deaths
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, already the worst in its history, has surpassed 9,000 cases with more than 4,000 deaths recorded since early October, according to health authorities.

stories.headline: Mauritius imposes curfew after police shooting sparks violent protests
stories.summary: Mauritius placed residents under curfew following rare violent unrest after a police officer shot and seriously wounded a woman.

stories.headline: Tinubu shuffles the generals as Boko Haram talks muddy the war plan
stories.summary: Africa Confidential reports that Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has reshuffled top military commanders even as negotiations with Boko Haram complicate the government's military strategy.

stories.headline: Microsoft closes its Nairobi hub
stories.summary: TechCabal reports Microsoft is shutting down its Nairobi hub, a significant pullback for one of Africa's biggest tech investment hubs, alongside other items including a UK fintech license confirmation and corporate earnings news.

stories.headline: As war with Ethiopia looms, how much weaponry does Eritrea have?
stories.summary: The Africa Report examines Eritrea's military capacity amid growing fears of renewed conflict with Ethiopia, questioning Asmara's ability to sustain a prolonged war.

stories.headline: South Africa remains premier mining jurisdiction, says Anglo American
stories.summary: Mining Weekly reports South Africa remains one of the world's premier mining jurisdictions, Anglo American has spelt out emphatically, amid itself investing R11.2-billion in an iron-ore project at Sishen.

Africa.gaps: The Continent's most recent available material was from late August 2026, too old for this window, so no current lead could be confirmed. African Business's newest visible items dated to roughly October 6-8, outside the 24-48 hour window. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and had no Africa-specific items in the provided feeds, so their current Africa coverage could not be verified.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by China's blockbuster September trade data showing a record-bound surplus, alongside a cluster of political and espionage stories — a UK spying probe tied to China, a high-profile corruption investigation, and a purge-adjacent probe of a former Bo Xilai ally — plus signs of cooling China-EU trade friction and PLA naval activity in the Pacific.

stories.headline: China's Exports Surge to Fastest Pace in Years, Trade Surplus on Record Pace
stories.summary: China's exports grew last month at the fastest pace in almost any month since the financial crisis, keeping the country's trade surplus on track to set a new record for the year. Bloomberg data shows <cite index="1-1,1-3,1-4">China's trade surplus ballooned to $938 billion for the first nine months, with exports soaring 36% in September — the fastest since February — after a 25% rise in August, while imports jumped 31%.</cite>

stories.headline: China's export engine fires on all cylinders as Beijing eases trade friction
stories.summary: <cite index="8-3,8-4">Chips and cars fueled September's export surge as Beijing moved to cool trade tensions with key partners, with China's export machine continuing to fire on all cylinders, buoyed by strong semiconductor and automobile shipments.</cite> <cite index="8-1">The country is on track to exceed a $1 trillion trade surplus again in 2026.</cite>

stories.headline: UK accuses China of using academics to spy on tech research
stories.summary: Britain's security establishment has alleged that Chinese-linked academics were used to spy on AI and other sensitive technology research. <cite index="12-3">Beijing denies the allegations, while British universities are being urged to end any work with the implicated institute.</cite>

stories.headline: China probes Huang Qifan, former ally of disgraced Bo Xilai
stories.summary: <cite index="11-1">China probes Huang Qifan, former ally of disgraced Bo Xilai,</cite> adding to a string of anti-corruption investigations touching figures tied to past political scandals.

stories.headline: China and EU pledge to contain trade disputes after Beijing talks
stories.summary: Beijing and Brussels signaled a cooling in trade tensions, with the two sides reaching an understanding on hybrid-vehicle trade and agreeing to explore tariff cuts on certain goods within the WTO framework following talks in Beijing, according to a joint statement reported by Caixin.

stories.headline: China's Liaoning carrier heads to the Pacific as US, Japan prepare joint drills
stories.summary: The PLA Navy's Liaoning aircraft carrier has begun its second western Pacific drill series this year, timed to overlap with an expanded US-Japan military exercise, underscoring persistent regional security tensions.

China.gaps: The Wire China and China Media Project had no recent China-politics/economy items surfaced via search or feed; Sixth Tone's recent output was mostly culture/human-interest (e.g., tennis star's sponsor promotion, Shanghai mayor meeting on AI/tourism) rather than hard economic or political news. Reuters, AP, FT, WSJ and The Economist block search, and no China-specific items from them appeared in the provided feed.
